quote:
Bridges endure when they are built by the steady hand of truth, not by the frantic beat of broken promises.  

A narrow strait that demands a toll of silence will only be king until the wind of reason breathes through it.  

Armed drums resound on foreign soil, yet only a quiet heart can still the echo of their steel.  

When the economy's roots are sown in swift wind, the trees will bend, for steady growth is a patient tree, not a reckless reed.  

A court that turns away a plant’s plea to be law reminds us that nature chooses when to bloom, not the law’s rapid decree.  

The crash of a great wing leaves the earth with a grieving sigh, for the sky remembers the traveler that slipped away.  

The most precious fossil, draped in layer upon layer of time, teaches that true treasure lies not in wealth, but in the quiet rhythm of history.
quote_preview: Bridges endure when they are built by the steady hand of truth, not by the frantic beat of broken promises.
